## Runs 6–7 — SdH spot checks on both density sides (`sdh-spot-check`)

Raw Rxx(B) is shown before the B-detrended FFT. Both 1D runs completed at D ≈ 0 with a stable ≈9.9 nA drain current, no clipping, and sample temperature 1.165–1.292 K. Run 6 (electron, n = +3.2×10¹² cm⁻²) has usable oscillations: a ≈7 T feature and peaks around 15, 22, and 30 T, many close to its harmonics. The ≈30 T peak is below the geometry-prior F_L = 33.1 T but cannot yet be assigned a distinct pocket; the peak set changes relative amplitude with the FFT cutoff. Run 7 (hole, n = −1.2×10¹²) shows ≈5 and ≈12.4 T content, but the accessible hole density is too low for the investigation's reliable separation regime. The electron side therefore carries the fan. This is a decision to measure F(n), not a stacking verdict.

`sdh_onset` on run 6 is censored at the low edge for the slow ≈7 T component; higher-frequency content appears by ≈1.4–1.9 T. The fan will include lower field for the small tone while using FFT cutoffs that exclude background-dominated rows. Detrending/window sensitivity and a global density-scale fit remain analysis tasks after the fan.

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from hera.analysis import open_run, sdh_fft, luttinger_frequency

fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 7))
for j, (rid, n) in enumerate(((6, 3.2), (7, -1.2))):
    rr = open_run(Path('/home/hera/measurements/zack/20260822-vti-02/data') / str(rid))
    order = np.argsort(rr.col('magnet_field'))
    b = rr.col('magnet_field')[order]
    rxx = rr.col('sr1_X')[order] / 1e-8  # sr1 unity, I_bias = 10 nA
    drain = rr.col('sr0_X')[order] / -1e6
    ax = axs[j, 0]
    ax.plot(b, rxx, lw=.8)
    ax.set(xlabel='B (T)', ylabel='Rxx (Ω)', title=f'Run {rid}: n={n:+.1f}×10¹² cm⁻², D≈0')
    ax.grid(alpha=.2)
    ax.text(.02,.96,f'drain {np.median(drain)*1e9:.2f} nA; T {rr.col("T_sample").min():.3f}–{rr.col("T_sample").max():.3f} K',transform=ax.transAxes,va='top',fontsize=8)
    ax = axs[j,1]
    for cutoff, style in ((1.5,'-'),(2.0,'--')):
        f, sp = sdh_fft(rxx[:,None],b,b_range=(cutoff,10),bg_degree=5,log=False,nfft=4096)
        sp = sp[0]
        mask = (f>2)&(f<50)
        ax.plot(f[mask],sp[mask]/sp[mask].max(),style,label=f'B≥{cutoff} T')
    fl = float(luttinger_frequency(n*1e16))
    ax.axvline(fl,color='k',lw=1,alpha=.5,label=f'F_L={fl:.1f} T')
    ax.set(xlabel='frequency (T)',ylabel='relative FFT amplitude',xlim=(0,50),title='FFT (B detrend, Hann)')
    ax.legend(fontsize=8)
    ax.grid(alpha=.2)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

## HERA — Step 4: electron-side D ≈ 0 Landau fan (`landau-fan-vti`)

> **05:23** · landau-fan-vti: D=0, electron n +2.6..+3.2e12 (22), B +0.9..+8 T (100 uniform-1/B), sr1 50 uV, fast\_delay 2.1 s · **ETA ~08:38** (≈3h15m)

Runs 6–7 are complete (ana cells 14–15). Run 6 at n = +3.2×10¹² cm⁻² has a ≈7 T feature plus ≈15, 22, 30 T peaks, several near its harmonics; the one-density peak set does not identify a pocket count. The hole side is capped at |n| ≤1.27×10¹² by the TG validator and is in the investigation's low-density exception regime. I am taking the electron side, n = +2.6…+3.2×10¹² at calibrated D = 0 (run 5), to distinguish true branch trajectories from harmonics and compare the resulting F(n) to the ABAB/ABCA model and F_L.

**Design floor:** the model ABAB partner is 5.41 T at n = 2.6 and 7.31 T at 3.2; F_L,max = 33.1 T. B = 0.9→8 T gives Δ(1/B) = 0.986 T⁻¹, or 5.33 periods for the smallest model partner. 100 uniform-1/B rows give 0.00996 T⁻¹ spacing, 3.03 samples per F_L period at n_max. Twenty-two n points (Δn = 0.0286×10¹²) give 3.0 samples per fourfold LL spacing at 0.9 T. The 1/B resolution over the full window is ≈1.01 T; if the high-frequency tone only survives above 1.5 T, its usable resolution is ≈1.85 T. The fan is floored at n≥2.6; lower electron density would leave fewer than five periods for the ABAB partner and cannot support the same count claim. The upper 2 T of the spot check is excluded because it buys little extra 1/B span, costs ~15 min of ramp, and raises the low-n, high-B dynamic-range risk. Fixed sr1 50 µV (5 kΩ at 10 nA) inherits run 6; its 8 T Rxx was ≈400–500 Ω at n=3.2, so inspect the n=2.6 corner for clipping. `fast_delay=2.1 s` is 7τ at the recorded τ=0.3 s, 24 dB/oct; run 5's 63×66 gatemap took 81.2 min at 1 s fast delay, and runs 6–7 measured the field traverse. Estimated wall time ≈3 h 15 m, including the initial 0→0.9 T positioning ramp (~7 min), 0.9→8 T measured traverse (~52 min), 2200 gate points, row turnaround, and margin.

The cell prints temperature, vaporizer, field, gates, Si, magnet state, lock-in settings, and NPLC before moving; it stops on mismatch. It leaves B at 8 T for a possible measured return leg and parks TG/BG at zero. **Checkpoints:** inspect the first 2–3 rows for drain-current continuity, TG/BG leakage, railing and field tracking; then inspect rows near B≈2, 4, 6 T for emerging oscillations, clipping, and temperature drift. Abort on sustained leakage >1 nA or an instrument anomaly; any magnet interrupt requires an actual field readback before further moves. The FFT and stacking read follow the completed TSV in the ana notebook.

# === landau-fan-vti: D=0 electron, n=+2.6..+3.2e12, B=0.9..8 T, 100x22 ===
from sharpelab_nb.gates import calc_gate_voltages, calc_nD

# Session calibration from run 5: ratio data-calibrated, absolute scale geometry prior.
CAL = dict(c_tg=2.796e-3, c_bg=2.161e-3, n_offset=-0.0894, D_offset=-0.013)
ns = np.linspace(2.6, 3.2, 22)  # 1e12 cm^-2
Ds = np.zeros_like(ns)
Vtgs, Vbgs = calc_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset'])
B_vec = 1 / np.linspace(1 / 0.9, 1 / 8.0, 100)  # uniform inverse field, increasing B
assert len(B_vec) == 100 and np.all(np.diff(B_vec) > 0) and B_vec[-1] <= B_SESSION_CAP
assert np.all((Vtgs >= TG_MIN) & (Vtgs <= TG_MAX)) and np.all((Vbgs >= BG_MIN) & (Vbgs <= BG_MAX))
assert np.max(np.abs(np.array(calc_nD(Vtgs, Vbgs, CAL['c_tg'], CAL['c_bg'], CAL['n_offset'], CAL['D_offset']))[1])) < 1e-8
print(f'fan n {ns[0]:+.3f}..{ns[-1]:+.3f}e12; TG {Vtgs[0]:+.4f}..{Vtgs[-1]:+.4f} V; BG {Vbgs[0]:+.4f}..{Vbgs[-1]:+.4f} V; B {B_vec[0]:.3f}..{B_vec[-1]:.3f} T')

# Silent preconditions: handoff parked field and gates at zero; base T and Si gate unchanged.
assert_thermometry_live('T_sample', VTI.temp_logfile_candidates['T_sample'], max_age=15, max_period=12)
assert_thermometry_live('T_vaporizer', VTI.temp_logfile_candidates['T_vaporizer'], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T, _Tv, _B = T_sample(), T_vaporizer(), magnet.field()
_tg, _bg, _si = k_tg.volt(), k_bg.volt(), k_si()
_ps, _out = magnet.persistent_switch_on(), magnet.output_enabled()
_tau, _slope, _amp = sr1.time_constant(), sr1.filter_slope(), sr1.amplitude()
print(f'precondition T_sample={_T:.3f} K [1.0,1.5], T_vaporizer={_Tv:.3f} K [0.7,1.5], B={_B:+.4f} T [|B|<0.05]; TG={_tg:+.4f}, BG={_bg:+.4f}, Si={_si:+.4f} V [all≈0]; PS heater={_ps}, output={_out}; sr1 tau={_tau} s, slope={_slope} dB/oct, amplitude={_amp} V; NPLC TG/BG={k_tg.nplci()}/{k_bg.nplci()}, magnet settle={magnet.settle_s} s')
assert 1.0 <= _T <= 1.5 and 0.7 <= _Tv <= 1.5 and abs(_B) < 0.05
assert abs(_tg) < 0.02 and abs(_bg) < 0.02 and abs(_si) < 0.01
assert _ps and _out and abs(_tau - 0.3) < 0.01 and _slope == 24 and abs(_amp - 1.0) < 0.02
assert k_tg.nplci() == 1 and k_bg.nplci() == 1 and magnet.settle_s >= 3.0

# Fixed sensitivity; field positioning blocks until the target is reached.
sr1.sensitivity(50e-6)
print(f'sr1 fixed sensitivity={sr1.sensitivity()} V (5 kOhm at 10 nA); positioning field at {B_vec[0]:.3f} T')
magnet.field(float(B_vec[0]))
_Bp = magnet.field()
print(f'field positioned: actual {_Bp:.4f} T versus target {B_vec[0]:.4f} T')
assert abs(_Bp - B_vec[0]) < 0.02

mc = dict(meas_config); mc['Si (V)'] = _si; mc['sample_temperature:'] = _T
mc['comments'] = 'landau-fan-vti: electron D=0 run-5 cal, n +2.6..+3.2e12 (22), B +0.9..+8 T uniform 1/B (100), sr1 50uV, fast_delay 2.1s'
s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')
s.add_comment(f'electron D=0; n {ns[0]:+.3f}..{ns[-1]:+.3f}e12 cm^-2 ({len(ns)} points); B {B_vec[0]:+.3f}..{B_vec[-1]:+.3f} T ({len(B_vec)} uniform-1/B rows); run-5 cal c_bg/c_tg={CAL["c_bg"]/CAL["c_tg"]:.3f}, n_offset={CAL["n_offset"]:+.4f}e12, D_offset={CAL["D_offset"]:+.3f} V/nm; sr1 50uV, tau 0.3s, 24dB, fast_delay 2.1s')
s.ramp(k_bg.volt, float(Vbgs[0])); s.ramp(k_tg.volt, float(Vtgs[0]))
interruptible_sleep(10)

# Row layout: time, B, TG, BG, T_sample, I_TG, I_BG, sr0.X/P, sr1.X/P.
s.fp(T_sample).fp(k_tg.curr).fp(k_bg.curr)
s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.X); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.X)
s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr1.P); s.plot(k_tg.volt, sr0.P)
s.plot('time', T_sample)
s.plot('time', k_tg.curr); s.plot('time', k_bg.curr)
I_TRIP = 1e-9
def leak_guard(station, data):
    i_tg, i_bg = abs(float(data[5])), abs(float(data[6]))
    if i_tg > I_TRIP or i_bg > I_TRIP:
        print(f'LEAK TRIP B={float(data[1]):+.3f} T, n-line TG={float(data[2]):+.3f} V: |I_tg|={i_tg:.3e}, |I_bg|={i_bg:.3e} A')
        station.interrupt_requested = True
s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

try:
    s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1.0, fast_delay=2.1)
finally:
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    print(f'post-run readback: B={magnet.field():+.4f} T; TG={k_tg.volt():+.4f}, BG={k_bg.volt():+.4f} V; T_sample={T_sample():.3f} K')
